summary: A Go HTTP API on the standard library with JSON resources, consistent errors, request logs and graceful shutdown.
description: Write a Go HTTP service on net/http's own router, with no web framework. One in-memory resource proves the shape: list, read and create routes, JSON validation, a single error envelope for misses and wrong methods, request IDs, slog access logs, a body size limit and server timeouts. The binary stops cleanly on SIGINT or SIGTERM, and integration tests check that against the built server. The recipe picks no database, authentication or hosting; the in-memory store sits behind an interface a database can replace.
seoDescription: A Go HTTP API recipe on net/http with JSON validation, one error envelope, request logging, timeouts, graceful shutdown and race-enabled tests.

projectExamples.title: Internal inventory service
projectExamples.description: Illustrative: replace the notes resource with items and stock levels for other internal services to call. Persistence and access control are work the project still has to add.

projectExamples.title: Webhook receiver in a container
projectExamples.description: Illustrative: accept JSON callbacks from a third-party service, validate them and log each request. Signature checks are custom work; docker-deploy builds and publishes the image.

plain.whatItIs: A starter web service written in Go that answers requests with JSON data, with clear error messages, request logs and a clean shutdown.
goodAt: Backends that a website or phone app calls to read and save records

Small services that report errors in one consistent format and log each request
notGoodAt: Projects that need a database or sign-in from the start; you add both yourself.
Pages and screens for people to click through; use a web app stack for those.
